description: All 40 chapters. F001-F007 dialogue migrated with deity voice keys remapped to MG-DEITY ids; F008 skeletons pending dialogue drafts.

chapters.title: Sun-Scale Threshold
chapters.codex: The Aten Hand-Ray Vestibule once blessed travelers before the Collapse. Now it judges them. The Sun-Scale Gate tests whether your law survives being weighed.

chapters.title: The Ma'at Scale Hall
chapters.codex: The Ma'at Scale Hall tests proportion. The Hollow scale-wraiths drain the deity's strongest ability first, forcing adaptation.

chapters.title: The Khepri Dawn Loop
chapters.codex: The Khepri Dawn Loop Chamber replays the first dawn endlessly. The Gate tests adaptability: can you win when every move you have already made becomes a weapon used against you?

chapters.title: The Hidden-Sun Archive
chapters.codex: The Hidden-Sun Archive stores pre-Collapse records. The most dangerous true history: the Gate predates the deities. They did not create it. They found it.

chapters.title: The Misweighed Dawn Judge
chapters.codex: The Misweighed Dawn Judge is a Hollow entity that consumed enough Ma'at law to issue verdicts in the Sun Realm's own voice. Its defeat proves: consumption is the opposite of balance.

chapters.title: Storm-Oath Threshold
chapters.codex: The Storm-Oath Bridge tests whether oaths have weight. The Hollow oath-eaters consume promises embedded in the bridge stones.

chapters.title: The Banner That Forgot Its King
chapters.codex: The Forgotten Banner carries the memory of a pre-Collapse king who swore to hold the bridge and failed. The Hollow oath-eaters use its testimony to create doubt, and doubt is terrain that dissolves.

chapters.title: Marble Law, Iron Oath
chapters.codex: The cross-faction collision zone is where Olympian trial law and Asgardian oath law both claim authority. The Hollow victory parasites imitate both systems simultaneously.

chapters.title: The Bridge Remembers Blood
chapters.codex: The Storm-Oath Bridge replays old dead vows as terrain pressure. Every oath ever broken on it rises as a ghost. The bridge does not forget.

chapters.title: The Forgotten Standard Bearer
chapters.codex: The Forgotten Standard Bearer is a Hollow entity wearing the armor of the first Asgardian oath-keeper. It can void any oath. Victory requires holding the bridge through action alone.

chapters.title: Laurel-Sky Threshold
chapters.codex: The Laurel-Sky Gate reopens as a trial arena. It tests whether excellence serves anything beyond itself. The laurel-bound champions are echoes of Olympians who entered with power but without purpose.

chapters.title: Oracle Vapor Corruption
chapters.codex: The oracle vapors have thickened into a weapon. They show futures the Gate wants you to believe. The oracle-maddened shades are former seers consumed by false visions.

chapters.title: The Forgotten Banner Testifies
chapters.codex: The Forgotten Banner carries the memory of a pre-Collapse war both sides deny starting. The Hollow victory parasites exploit the jurisdictional chaos by imitating both legal systems.

chapters.title: The Trial Road Fractures
chapters.codex: The trial road fractures into zones where different legal codes hold. The Gate chooses one law: excellence must be witnessed by the Gate itself — but a broken witness sees nothing clearly.

chapters.title: The Thunder Tribunal Usurper
chapters.codex: The Thunder Tribunal Usurper is a Hollow entity wearing the shape of a forgotten Olympian-Asgardian judge. It weighs. Every judgment has physical weight. Victory requires proving excellence has purpose beyond ego.

chapters.title: Torii-Moon Threshold
chapters.codex: The Torii-Moon Gate reopens as a distortion gate. Reflections move before their owners. The shrine-path tests attention, not power.

chapters.title: The False Reflection
chapters.codex: The Mirror Lake reflects what the Gate wants you to believe, not what is. False reflections fight with copied abilities but without copied conviction.

chapters.title: Storm Behind the Torii
chapters.codex: The Gate's distortion has bled the Stormmoot storm into the shrine-path, creating a hybrid terrain of torii gates that act as storm-bridges.
chapters.migration_note: originality pass: real-myth vocabulary (Kami/Asgardian) replaced with original nomenclature

chapters.title: The Boundary Weakens
chapters.codex: The Gate's distortion thins the boundary between material and spirit. The Hollow boundary-thieves pull the spirit out of the body, leaving a hollow shell.

chapters.title: The False Reflection Sovereign
chapters.codex: The False Reflection Sovereign is the Gate's most perfect imitation. Victory requires using the boundary itself — proving that the threshold between material and spirit still has authority.
chapters.migration_note: originality pass: real-myth vocabulary (Kami/Asgardian) replaced with original nomenclature

chapters.title: Silver-Root Threshold
chapters.codex: The Silver-Root Gate reopens beneath the oldest grove in Avalora. The Hollow root-rot drains memory from living terrain, making roots forget what they were holding.

chapters.title: The Geas Labyrinth
chapters.codex: The geas labyrinth is a living maze grown from ancient promises and bloodline debts. The Hollow changelings corrupt terrain memory. Navigation requires reading the terrain, not trusting the path.

chapters.title: Beast Realm Predation
chapters.codex: Beast Realm predators nest in wounded roots that also hold the Gate stable. The Tuatha must fight without destroying the terrain, asking whether the forest can reject creatures that are part of its ecosystem.

chapters.title: The Scar That Remembers
chapters.codex: The scar from the original Ascension Collapse has never healed. The Hollow weaponizes grief by creating copies of lost deities. They are ghosts. Fighting them requires witnessing grief without becoming part of it.

chapters.title: The Crow-Crowned Geas Breaker
chapters.codex: The Crow-Crowned Geas Breaker breaks oaths rather than attacking directly. Victory requires winning without making any promises. The forest chooses to hold the Gate. The deity asks.

chapters.title: Choir-Vault Threshold
chapters.codex: The Choir-Vault Gate reopens with dissonance. The choir husks are former Empyrean corrected into emptiness — what the Empyrean become when preservation removes everything that does not match the song.

chapters.title: Memory-Burn Radiance
chapters.codex: The Gate leaks memory-burning radiance — light that erases what it illuminates. The question: what remains when memory is stripped — instinct, or emptiness? The Empyrean answer: conviction.

chapters.title: The Dissonant Choir
chapters.codex: The Empyrean choir has fractured. The Broken Engine Leviathan is a Hollow entity made from fused choir fragments that consumes any voice trying to rejoin the original song.

chapters.title: The Glass Stair War
chapters.codex: The glass stairway is the vault's ascent path. The Hollow stair-phantoms create false steps. The bell shockwaves make the heaviest combatant fall. Victory requires climbing by sound, not by sight.

chapters.title: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise
chapters.codex: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise attacks with silence. Victory requires embracing dissonance — proving that imperfection is not a flaw to be corrected but a feature of being alive.

chapters.title: Black-Iron Threshold
chapters.codex: The Black-Iron Gate reopens with a contract of entry written in fire. The Hollow clause-eaters consume the contract text to create loopholes. A contract without terms is a debt without limit.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.codex: The Debt Ledger records every Gate transaction, including pre-Collapse debts. The False Pact Wardens weaponize the ledger, charging the deity for every action taken.

chapters.title: Ash Market
chapters.codex: The Ash Market is a pre-Collapse trading post that still functions. The unique feature: trading debt onto Hollow entities. Every trade creates a new relationship — and in the Dominion, relationships are chains.

chapters.title: The Execution Sigil Crisis
chapters.codex: The Hollow clause-eaters rewrite the Gate's contract clauses, turning every execution sigil against the deity. The Ash Court Usurper uses Dominion law as a weapon. The only counter: rewrite the sigils mid-combat, choosing when to be vulnerable.

chapters.title: The Volcanic Glass Magistrate
chapters.codex: The Volcanic Glass Magistrate has no interest in truth — only collection. Victory requires proving the court's own authority is a debt it cannot justify — because the court was created by a contract the Hollow has already eaten. The debt is void because the creditor no longer legally exists.

chapters.title: Deepgreen Threshold
chapters.codex: the Gate opens in fog; the oldest faction answers slowest
